newsitem.title: USA: Wall St seen opening lower on pre-election anxiety.
newsitem.headline: Wall St seen opening lower on pre-election anxiety.

text.p: U.S. stocks were expected to open lower on Monday with anxious investors sticking to the sidelines, worried about a possible Democratic sweep of both houses of Congress in Tuesday's U.S. elections.
"It looks like a lower opening," said Peter Cardillo, director of research at Westfalia Investments.
The 30 year benchmark treasury bond was off 6/32, yielding 6.69 percent and Standard & Poor's December futures fell 0.35 to 706.15 ahead of Monday's opening.

With many seeing victory for President Bill Clinton as a foregone conclusion in the presidential race, market analysts were turning their eyes to the Congressional races and speculating whether voters would upset Republican control of the House and Senate.
"It's going to be very cautious because if the Democrats take Congress, that would be very negative for the stock market. We could see a 10 to 15 percent drop if that happened," Cardillo said.
